options.name: 1. Add a scrollbar variable to the resolver in configs/browsers.ts (recommended)
options.mechanism: `resolveBrowser` reads one more operator variable, for example `PLAYWRIGHT_SCROLLBARS=classic` (the name is for the names rule to settle). When it is set, the resolver merges `ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--hide-scrollbars']` into whatever `launchOptions` the precedence chain returns. That covers the executable, channel, managed, bundled, and system branches, and the pinned case, which goes from `{}` to `{ launchOptions: { ignoreDefaultArgs } }`. With `PLAYWRIGHT_WS_ENDPOINT` the server owns the launch, so the variable either refuses that pair or is documented as a no-op there. vite.config.ts:23 already forwards the result to every project, so no factory changes. The proofs' queue command sets the variable and also passes `--mode classic`, which engages the control that already exists at Lock.test.ts:153. On this host the command is `flock /home/user/.wave/journey.lock env PLAYWRIGHT_SCROLLBARS=classic npx vitest run --config vite.config.ts --no-cache --mode classic --project src:browser tests/src/browser/Lock.test.ts tests/src/browser/Modal.test.ts tests/src/browser/Offcanvas.test.ts`, with `PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE_PATH` added for 153. The executable branch and the variable compose.

The classic run is therefore an operator or queue command, not part of `npm test`, and in the standing gate the gutter cases read width 0. recommendation:
Take option 1: add an optional scrollbar variable to `resolveBrowser` in configs/browsers.ts. When it is set, the resolver merges `ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--hide-scrollbars']` into whatever launch options the existing precedence chain returns. Run the gutter proofs with that variable plus `--mode classic`, so the control that already exists at tests/src/browser/Lock.test.ts:153 requires a nonzero measured width. Restrict the command to Lock.test.ts, Modal.test.ts, and Offcanvas.test.ts under the queue (`flock /home/user/.wave/journey.lock env PLAYWRIGHT_SCROLLBARS=classic npx vitest run --config vite.config.ts --no-cache --mode classic --project src:browser ...`).

It is the least configuration because it adds no file, no project, no instance, and no factory parameter. It edits only the leaf that already owns every launch option (configs/browsers.ts:289-315) and already reads three `PLAYWRIGHT_*` operator overrides (:295-306). vite.config.ts:23 already forwards the leaf's result to every browser project, and `--mode` already reaches the proofs through `mergeOverride` (vite.config.ts:85-91). When the variable is unset, every standing gate and every other generated workspace launches exactly as it does at scaffold 0.0.93. D3 measured 15 px with this exact launch shape (codex/browser-stage-b-design-verdict.md:206, :211).

The costs:
- **Scaffold release.** configs/browsers.ts is scaffold content and byte-identical to the 0.0.93 template, so the edit lands in the scaffold template (src/core/templates.ts), its resolver cases (tests/src/core/templates.test.ts:1693-1709), and the precedence prose (guides/scaffold.md:2095-2103). Then a release and a veneer overwrite follow. B3's gutter half waits on that release.
- **Separate command.** The classic run is an operator or queue command outside `npm test`, because no cross-platform package script can set the variable inline.
- **Unmeasured hosts.** The first classic run has to establish two things: a nonzero width on Linux Chromium 141 and 153, and that the other cases in Modal.test.ts and Offcanvas.test.ts hold at that width.

Rulings on the other options:
- **Option 4** (the existing WebSocket endpoint with a server launched without the flag) changes no configuration. It adds a server process and launcher on every run and leaves the instrument outside any tested configuration.
- **Options 2 and 3** each edit the root factory.
- **Options 5, 6, and 7** each fail on platform, measurement, or host grounds.
